paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: This image displays a nested donut chart representing the distribution of samples across two ambiguity metrics, featuring two concentric rings that contain a total of seven slices. Two legends are provided on the right: one for "Ambiguity Std (Outer)" and another for "Max Ambiguity (Inner)". Percentage labels are overlaid directly inside each segment in bold text, though none of the slices are exploded or further offset for visual emphasis. The outer ring contains four slices: "Std: 0.0" in dark blue representing 49.0%, "Std: 0.47" in medium blue at 39.0%, "Std: 0.82" in standard blue at 7.0%, and "Std: 0.94" in bright blue at 5.0%. The inner ring is composed of three slices: "Max: 1" in bright blue accounting for 47.7%, "Max: 2" in a lighter blue at 38.0%, and "Max: 3" in the lightest blue making up 14.2%. The slices in both rings are not arranged in a strict ascending or descending order by size.
